comparator.sourceNotes: UvA distinguishes the English Global Communication Science track from Dutch Communicatiewetenschap. The English study-programme table supplies 60 EC in each year. Year 1 contains seven compulsory courses (12+12+6+6+8+8+8 EC). Year 2 contains five 6-EC theory/research/practice courses, a 24-EC internationally oriented internship and a 6-EC internship case. Year 3 combines 30 EC of genuine open elective/minor/exchange space, one 6-EC communication-topic restricted elective, an 18-EC independent research project and 6 EC From Research to Impact. The named topic examples are not assigned as compulsory content; the 6-EC restricted choice is retained generically.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The audience-strategy route adds Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Consumer Product Design, Market Research, International Business & Governance and Leadership & Diversity Management, while the broad route instead studies cross-border political crises, media archaeology, environmental media, sociology and youth extremism. More than four courses differ in each direction, changing the programme from global-public media analysis to communication decisions in international organisations.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad route covers media effects, cross-cultural differences, global issues and research. The official marketing and organisation theme plus direct target-specific interests support a distinct applied strategy route. A third health-and-sustainability communication route has only a small number of direct UCR communication courses; filling 24 places would convert it into health or sustainability study rather than retain communication science as the organising field. Stop at two.

notes.text: UvA provides a continuous empirical communication-science sequence, compulsory 24-EC international internship and 18-EC research project. UCR combines media and rhetoric with research methods, psychology and applied settings, but does not reproduce a compulsory communication placement, content-analysis/statistical sequence or independent communication-science project. Its optional independent research element is a separate opportunity outside the scheduled 180 EC.
